# Cross-language golden for the uptime ladder. Three implementations render it
# — state.UptimeDur (Go), _sl_uptime_dur (bash) and dwuptime (jq, inside `sl
# status`) — because the Go CLI, the bash fallback and a jq program cannot
# share code. This file is what keeps them the same rule rather than three
# rules that happen to agree today.
#
# Go asserts against it in TestUptimeDurGolden; bash and jq in
# scripts/check-uptime-parity.sh, which `make check` runs.
#
# Every handover point, and — at each level — a major of 5-9 with a non-zero
# minor next to the first double-digit major. That pair is the collapse
# threshold, and it is the number most likely to be tweaked by someone who
# finds one of these readings too terse. Without it a table can look thorough
# and still pass with the rule changed: the first draft of this file had
# nothing above 3d3h, and moving the cutoff from 10 to 5 did not fail it.
#
# It also carries, at each level that renders NO minor unit, a case with a
# large residual in the unit below (90 = 1m30s, 570 = 9m30s, 3570 = 59m30s).
# Without those, a rule that starts appending the smaller unit under some
# condition — "seconds when minutes < 10 and seconds >= 30" — passes every
# case in the table while changing what users see.
#
# And, at every level, a major of exactly 10 with a NON-ZERO minor: 37800
# (10h30m), 900000 (10d10h), 26352000 (10mo5d), 340000000 (10y11mo). A case
# whose minor happens to be zero cannot pin this — 36000 and 36030 are both
# 10h0m, so "collapse at 10" and "collapse at 11" render them identically.
# That was a real hole: the first attempt at this file added 36030 believing
# it closed the gap, and it did not.
#
# Format: <seconds> <want>.
-5 0s
0 0s
1 1s
45 45s
59 59s
60 1m
61 1m
90 1m
312 5m
570 9m
3540 59m
3570 59m
3599 59m
3600 1h
3601 1h
3660 1h1m
3900 1h5m
7200 2h
7260 2h1m
19800 5h30m
35940 9h59m
36000 10h
36030 10h
37800 10h
46920 13h
86399 23h
86400 1d
90000 1d1h
100000 1d3h
270000 3d3h
475200 5d12h
863940 9d23h
864000 10d
864030 10d
900000 10d
950400 11d
2591999 29d
2592000 1mo
2592030 1mo

13564800 5mo7d
25919999 9mo29d
25920000 10mo
